REFERRED TO CRIME VICTIMS, CRIME AND CORRECTION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the correction law and the public health law, in relation to
birth certificates for inmates
items.lawCode: Amd §§71, 125 & 201, Cor L; amd §§4174 & 4179, Pub Health L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2855

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law and the public health law, in
relation to birth certificates for inmates

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To ensure the accuracy of inmate birth certificates and to ensure
persons released from prison have state-issued identification.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends section 71 of the correction law to codi-
fy the existing practice of the Department of Corrections of obtaining
birth certificates and social security cards for inmates, providing then
to the inmate upon his or her release from prison.

Section one also required the Department of make best efforts to have an
inmate's birth certificate corrected when the certificate contains an
error or is incomplete.

Section two of the bill amends section 125 of the correction law to
codify the existing practice of providing a Department issued photo
identification card to each inmate upon release.

Section three of the bill amends section 201 of the correction law to
provide the discretion to community supervision officers to have a
releasee's expiring Department identification card reissued when neces-
sary to ensure uninterrupted possession of identification while the
releasee is making efforts to meet the documentation requirements of the
Department of Motor Vehicles.

Sections four and five of the bill amends the public health health law
to add corrections and amendments to birth certificates to those docu-
ments provided to the Department of Corrections at no charge.

Section six is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Currently the Department of Corrections works to obtain birth certif-
icates and social security cards for inmates, furnishing the documents
to them upon their release. The Department does this in part so that
releasees can quickly obtain department of motor vehicle identification
cards. Sometimes, however, a birth certificate contains a spelling error
or is missing information, such as the inmate's first name, largely
rendering it useless for the purpose of obtaining a DMV identification
card. Getting a birth certificate corrected can be a long and arduous
process and is particularly difficult for a person just getting out of
prison who does not have other forms of identification.

This bill would require the Department to make best efforts to assist
such inmates in having their birth certificates corrected and reissued
while they are still in prison.


Additionally, the Department provides inmates photo identification cards
upon their release, so that they have some form of identification while
they work to obtain housing, employment and identification from the DMV.
The Department's release identification requires fingerprinting and
scanning of the inmate's image into the state's facial recognition soft-
ware database, in addition to the traditional security features of a
state-issued identification card.  However, these prison-issued iden-
tification cards expire 90 days after release, which may occur before a
releasee has obtained a nondrivers identification card from DMV. Where a
releasee might need a few more weeks to gather and/or obtain DMV-re-
quired documents, this bill will allow community supervision officers
the discretion to reissue a releasee's prison-issued identification card
for an additional period of time to be determined by the Department.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.4212 of 2019-20; Advanced to Third Reading
Assembly: Ordered to third reading in 2014, 2015, 2016.
Reported to Ways and Means, 2018, 2019.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become law

BILL NUMBER: S2855A

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law and the public health law, in
relation to birth certificates for incarcerated individuals

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To ensure the accuracy of incarcerated individual's birth certificates
and to ensure persons released from prison have state-issued identifica-
tion.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends subdivision (a) of section 601 of the
correction law authorizing the Department of Corrections to request a
certified copy of a birth certificate on half of an incarcerated indi-
vidual from Department of Health.

Section two of the bill amends section 71 of the correction law to codi-
fy the existing practice of the Department of Corrections of obtaining
birth certificates and social security cards for incarcerated individ-
uals, providing them to the incarcerated individual upon his or her
release from prison.

Section two also requires the Department of make best efforts to have an
incarcerated individual's birth certificate corrected when the certif-
icate contains an error or is incomplete.

Section three of the bill amends section 125 of the correction law to
codify the existing practice of providing a Department issued photo
identification card to each incarcerated individual upon release.

Section four of the bill amends section 201 of the correction law to
provide the discretion to community supervision officers to have a

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.4212 of 2019-20; Advanced to Third Reading Assembly: Ordered to third
reading in 2014, 2015, 2016. Reported to Ways and Means, 2018, 2019.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law; provided however, that the amendments to subdi-
vision (a) of section 601 of the correction law made by section one of
this act shall not affect the expiration of such subdivision and shall
be deemed to expire therewith.

summary: Relates to birth certificates for incarcerated individuals; requires birth certificate or certification of birth, or certified transcript of birth and social security card to be kept in the incarcerated individual's records until the incarcerated individual is released from custody when such birth certificate or certification of birth, or certified transcript of birth and social security card shall be provided to the incarcerated individual.
